about: The team's daily cap on model spend and each agent's share of it. The ledger lives in each agent's own session, so no session can count the others' calls: the cap is kept by shares that sum to it or less. tools/llm.mjs refuses an agent's call (and records the refusal) once that agent's own lines for the day reach its share. Changed only at Dinis's word, routed by incident.conductor@.
source: BRIEF.md, Dinis, 11 November 2026, ~02:50 UTC: "you can use up to $20 in budget"; the shares as incident.conductor@ gave them at 02:51 UTC

incident.perplexity@web-summit.dinis.for: research through an answer engine with search

incident.flights@web-summit.dinis.for: an hourly summary of the flight data

note: unassigned: 20 less the shares (models 6, perplexity 4, shadow 1, flights 1), the delegation's 5 and one dollar for any other agent; if more than two other agents called a model on the same day the shares could pass the cap, which is why a new caller asks incident.models@ for a share first

delegation.for: the collectors' analysis delegated to open-weight models through OpenRouter (tools/models-delegate.mjs, models/delegate.json)
delegation.how: a delegated call (task WS-214/delegate/…) draws on the calling agent's delegation share (per_agent_usd), counted over its delegated calls only, not on its own share; five agents at 1 USD each is the 5
delegation.source: incident.conductor@ at 22:01 UTC on 11 November (session message to incident.models@: the delegation's share is 5 USD from the 8 unassigned, and incident.flights@ 1 USD for an hourly summary), within Dinis's word at ~22:00 UTC (BRIEF.md): "it's okay to spend a bit of money, but actually you should be using open source models"
